prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1361; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a sideswipe while changing lanes and described a knee injury from the impact. The claim was opened and the file assigned for review.

Entry 2: Photos taken at the scene confirm several details of the reported damage to the side panels. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the photos are the main visual record at this stage.

Entry 3: The damage to the vehicle is mostly in line with the impact described by the claimant. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.

Entry 4: The driver is named on the policy. Police records and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the incident.

Entry 5: The claimant gave the same account in every conversation so far. The knee injury is plausible for a collision of this type, and no earlier injury to the same body area is known.

Entry 6: Medical treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer and has been dealing with the claim directly.

Entry 7: Based on the photos, the vehicle damage, the medical course and the consistent account, the claim appears consistent with the reported incident and remains open pending final review of the medical and repair records.
